summary.intent: Execute Phase 59 of the GSD workflow (FUSE IPNS verify/publish hardening and cleanup) — 4 plans in a strict sequential dependency chain, all Rust, TDD mode on.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (plan 59-01) fully landed with 95 passing tests after recovering a SUMMARY.md commit lost to a 522 error; the session switched from worktree to sequential execution for Waves 2–4, and Wave 2 was dispatched at transcript end.

repo: Phase 59 is a strict sequential chain (59-01→02→03→04); no plan can run until the prior merges.
Root `npm test` runs `pnpm --parallel -r run test` (full monorepo) — RAM-starving for a Rust-only phase; post-merge gate must be scoped to `cargo` on `cipherbox-fuse` only.
winfsp feature builds are CI-only on macOS; crypto-clippy warnings are pre-existing — both are known non-blockers.
The cleanup-wave helper fails closed on untracked files in the worktree (e.g. a node_modules symlink), preventing merge until they're removed.
The tracking commit helper prints `commit_failed` as a false-negative even when the commit actually lands — do not retry.

code.finding: Finding A (59-01): `build_folder_metadata` was swallowing `wrap_key` errors and publishing a FilePointer with `ipns_private_key_encrypted: None`, making the file permanently unrecoverable.
Finding B (59-01): inode resolution was not re-triggered when `file_meta_ipns_name` changed under an unchanged mtime, causing stale CID/key reads.

Finding C (59-02): `VerifyError::Legacy` was a unit variant; needed migration to `Legacy { cid: String, sequence_number: String }` across 9 match-arm sites in 6 files to eliminate a redundant second resolve_ipns call and close a race window.

workflow: Worktree isolation only pays off for concurrent parallel executors; sequential single-plan waves have no parallelism to isolate and only add merge/cleanup overhead.
GSD #2070: executor writes SUMMARY.md but the worktree is force-removed before that file is committed → summary permanently lost. Sequential mode eliminates this failure mode.
When a subagent worktree genuinely needs node_modules, it must run `pnpm i` to initialize its own copy — never symlink back to the parent checkout.
The cleanup-wave `mktemp` template must be unique per invocation; reuse causes an empty manifest variable and a silent no-op merge.

friction: Two Cloudflare 522 errors: one mid-Wave-1 subagent run (nearly lost the SUMMARY.md commit), one during the worktree merge step.
Worktree execution was activated unnecessarily for a fully sequential phase — added merge/cleanup overhead with no benefit.
cleanup-wave helper failed with an empty `--manifest` due to a `mktemp` template collision; required manual path fix.
cleanup-wave rejected the worktree merge because the subagent had created an untracked `node_modules` symlink back to the parent tree.
Tracking commit helper emitted a false `commit_failed` message even though the commit succeeded, creating momentary confusion.
open_items: GSD workflow default could detect single-plan-per-wave sequential chains and skip worktree isolation automatically rather than requiring manual override.
